title: Spurs climb to No. 2 in latest rankings
heading: 2003-04 Power Rankings: Week 8

rankings.summaryHtml: It probably isn't much consolation, but losing to Dallas seems to have tripped up the hated Mavs' season as much as it helped them, judging by Dallas' week.
rankings.summaryText: It probably isn't much consolation, but losing to Dallas seems to have tripped up the hated Mavs' season as much as it helped them, judging by Dallas' week.

rankings.summaryHtml: Rasho's D can't be that bad, because Spurs have held the opposition under 80 points 13 times already ... and they're 13-0 in those games.
rankings.summaryText: Rasho's D can't be that bad, because Spurs have held the opposition under 80 points 13 times already ... and they're 13-0 in those games.

rankings.summaryHtml: It's a good thing they're playing so well without Webber. Because he's going to end up missing more time than anyone expected, Webb included.

rankings.summaryHtml: Not fully healthy yet (Wally) and not winning at home yet (7-5), but Wolves are starting to show us glimpses of the good squad they're supposed to be.

rankings.summaryHtml: 7-0 record after a loss is admirable -- no one in the league can match it -- but 6-6 record since 14-2 start is more than a little disconcerting.

rankings.summaryHtml: Relying on your offense is fine, but the plan doesn't work when your FG and FT shooting slip noticeably and the road -- 3-9 after a league-leading mark of 27-14 last season -- starts to look as tough as it did during the extremely dark 1990s.

rankings.summaryHtml: Honestly, I don't know how the computer allowed the Grizz up here. Hubie, meanwhile, gets points for honesty, but I'm not so sure it's smart to say publicly that a team is playing 10 guys instead of eight to build up everyone's trade value.

rankings.summaryHtml: Our poor pal Frank Hughes can't go anywhere without someone bringing up his prediction that Jazz would only win nine games. Fact is, the only thing 'worst' about this scrappy bunch is Kirilenko's haircut, which makes Steve Nash look stylin'.

rankings.summaryHtml: Ever so briefly, Nets were over .500 (13-12) for first time since they were 2-1. Not surprisingly, the good cheer felt around the club was also brief.

rankings.summaryHtml: Dunleavy might barely crack most folks' top 5 among Coach of the Year candidates in his own conference. But he's not far off the pace set by Bzdelik, Sloan, Hubie and J. Van Gundy, winning consistently with a stripped-down Clipper ship.

rankings.summaryHtml: We warned you not to get too geeked up about the 5-0 start post-trade. Last six games (1-5) prove committee right yet again.
